answer: Synchronized cohort timing locks. Identities join random cohorts and must return signed round-trip echoes inside a tight window; a miss voids the identity and consumes a nonrefundable coordination credit. Cohorts are redrawn at the demand zenith, forcing concurrent online presence and real compute. Relay paths rotate across a reef of independent nodes, so cached replies fail. The rule is a simple fable: be present together or pay. Attacker cost per identity is sustained uptime, unique relay capacity, and synchronization latency every cycle.
